hypothesis: If the H65-1 knickpoint signal was inflated by the brief's named confounds (playa/pluvial shoreline, basin fill, conductive ground-water discharge, ephemeral low-area channels), then applying those confound masks to the statistic itself should change the first-test verdict; the masked statistic's withheld-crossing contrast still carries no fault signal (E1 stays INCONCLUSIVE) and the pooled holdout DTI stays far below the mass-matched random control.
mechanism: A fault offsets base level; the steepness contrast propagates upstream as a knickpoint (Kirby & Whipple 2012, J. Struct. Geol. 44, 54-75; Perron & Royden 2013, ESPL 38, 570-576; Gailleton et al. 2019, ESurf 7, 211-230). H66-1 additionally masks, from the channel-cell population entering the statistic, cells on playa, in basin fill, on high-conductance surface (ground-water discharge mimic), and in ephemeral channels (A < 1e6 m2), per the lane brief's mandated confound list.
mimicking_non_fault_process: The brief's named mimics, now MEASURED as masks: playa/pluvial shorelines (550,267 px), basin fill (516,432 px), conductive surface (257,039 px), ephemeral channels (317,451 px of the 786,299 channel px; 386,327 channel px excluded total). With all four masked, the masked first-test mean moved only from +0.0326 (H65-1, 262 comps) to +0.0404 (239 comps) and the CI still straddles zero: the confounds did not create the (non-)signal.
